offence_category.reason: Final conviction is for culpable homicide not amounting to murder under s.304 Part II, which fits the category.

statutory_provisions.reason: Charged sections (302/34, 201) and final sections (304 Part II/34, 201) match the judgment.

weapon.reason: The co-accused struck the head with a rod, which is the only weapon mentioned.

evidence_type.reason: Judgment mentions the chemical examiner report and general evidence on record; it does not detail witness types, and the value says so.

confession.reason: No confession or admission by the accused is mentioned.

aggravating_circumstances.reason: No aggravating facts are noted in the judgment.

mitigating_circumstances.reason: Sudden fight, no pre-meditation, no intention to kill, and over three years served (as submitted) are all in the judgment.

trial_court_outcome.reason: Sessions Court convicted under ss.302/34 and 201, with life RI and three years RI, plus fine, as stated.

final_outcome.reason: Supreme Court modified the conviction to s.304 Part II/34, which fits conviction_modified.

offence_finally_established.reason: Final convictions are s.304 Part II r/w s.34 and s.201, as stated.

imprisonment_type.reason: Final sentence is seven years rigorous imprisonment, a fixed term.

imprisonment_years.reason: Judgment sentences the appellant to seven years rigorous imprisonment.

fine_rs.reason: Fine of Rs.10,000 imposed by the High Court is maintained.

neutral_facts.correct_value: Summary of the incident without the court's characterisation; drop 'the scuffle took place on the spur of the moment' (a court finding) and keep the factual account of the quarrel, blow and body disposal.
neutral_facts.quote: The scuffle took place on the spur of the moment.
neutral_facts.reason: Facts are largely accurate, but 'spur of the moment' echoes the court's mitigating finding, leaning toward the outcome.

offence_severity.reason: The judgment does not state the statutory maximum or minimum punishment for the offence.

attempt_completion.reason: The victim died, so the offence was completed.

physical_harm.reason: Death from a rod blow to the head, with body moved to canal, matches the judgment.

number_of_offences.reason: Two sections charged (302/34 and 201) and two convictions stand in modified form.

financial_property_loss.reason: Alleged theft of the appellant's pigeon is the only property element; no value is given.

premeditation_planning.reason: Court expressly found the act was not pre-meditated and arose on the spur of the moment.

motive.reason: The court accepted the sudden quarrel over the alleged theft of the pigeon as the trigger.

key_evidence_accepted.reason: Evidence of sudden scuffle without intent to kill and the chemical examiner report on liquor are relied on, as stated.

witness_credibility.reason: The judgment does not assess witness credibility.

post_offence_conduct.reason: The judgment notes the body was shifted to the minor canal after no response for half an hour.

custody_duration.reason: No custody period is recorded; the parenthetical accurately reports counsel's submission about three years served.

bail_history.reason: No bail grant or refusal for this appellant is mentioned.

trial_duration.reason: High Court dates (08.02.2019, 01.03.2019) and Supreme Court date (21.09.2021) match; offence and trial dates are absent.

legal_representation.reason: Counsel for the appellant and State match the judgment's appearance list and submissions.

investigation_status.reason: The judgment states the accused were convicted by the Sessions Court after trial, supporting the value.

procedural_irregularity.reason: No procedural lapse is noted by the court.

appeal_history.reason: Outcomes at trial, High Court and Supreme Court match the judgment.

prosecution_argument.reason: State argued no grounds to interfere, leniency shown, and Uday Singh distinguishable on facts, as recorded.

defence_argument.reason: Defence argued no intention to kill, sudden heat-of-passion fight, reliance on Uday Singh, and sentence reduction request.

legal_principle_applied.reason: Court applied absence of intention to kill or cause such injury, leading to s.304 Part II rather than Part I.

precedent_relied_upon.reason: Uday Singh (2002) 7 SCC 79 and Shahajan Ali (2017) 11 SC 807 are the cases relied on, with citations matching.

sentencing_rationale.reason: Judgment ties conversion to absence of intention and sudden fight and gives no separate reasoning for seven years.

judicial_mitigating_factors.reason: Sudden fight in heat of passion, no pre-meditation and no intention to kill are the court's own factors.

judicial_aggravating_factors.reason: The court identifies no aggravating factors.
